Best Android TV box 2026: top picks compared

Spec sheets all say “8K, Wi-Fi 6, fast chip”. This guide picks one model per type of buyer and compares the specs that actually decide daily use. New to TV boxes? Start with theAndroid TV box buyer’s guide.

Last updated: October 30, 2026

On this pageHow we pickedQuick comparisonThe picksWhat to avoidFAQ

How we picked

  • Chipset first, brand second. Newer platforms (such as Amlogic S905X5M / S905Y5, Rockchip RK3576 / RK3539, Allwinner H728) run current Android versions well. Older budget chips are fine for light use only.
  • RAM decides how smooth it feels. 4GB is the comfortable choice for a main TV with many apps. 2GB suits a bedroom or travel TV.
  • Network matters more than marketing. Wi-Fi 6 helps in crowded networks, but a strong 5GHz Wi-Fi 5 signal beats a weak Wi-Fi 6 one. Gigabit Ethernet mainly helps with large local files.
  • Android version. Every pick below runs Android 14 according to its product specs.
  • Specs come from our catalog. Every value in the table is read from the live product data when this page is built. Always confirm variants and current price on the product page.

The picks

1. Best overall value: X96Q M200

Best for: Everyday 4K streaming box with Wi-Fi 6 and wired Gigabit

A current Amlogic S905X5M platform on Android 14, with Wi-Fi 6 and Gigabit Ethernet listed in the specs. Configurations run from 2GB + 16GB up to 4GB + 64GB, so you can pick the 4GB versions for a living-room daily driver.

Buy it if: you want one modern, balanced box for the main TV and prefer a wired connection when it is available.

2. Premium / most powerful: H96 MAX M9

Best for: Heavy multitasking, big local media libraries, NAS playback

The Rockchip RK3576 is an 8-core chip (4 × Cortex-A72 + 4 × Cortex-A53) with a Mali-G52 MC3 GPU and a 6 TOPS NPU. The 8GB + 128GB configuration gives the most headroom in this list, and the specs list HDMI 2.1, Wi-Fi 6, Gigabit Ethernet and USB 3.0.

Video output (as listed): HDMI 2.1, 8K

Buy it if: you play large local files, keep many apps installed, or simply want the most headroom. The near-identical H96 MAX M9S is an alternative.

3. Compact modern Amlogic: Tanix TX5 Plus

Best for: A second TV or bedroom with HDR10+ content

Same S905X5M generation as the X96Q M200, on Android 14, with 4K@60fps and HDR10+ output listed. It ships as 2GB + 16GB with Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0 and has one USB 3.0 port.

Video output (as listed): HDMI, 4K@60fps, HDR10+

Buy it if: you want a newer Amlogic chip and HDR10+ support for lighter, single-app use.

4. Budget box with Wi-Fi 6 + Gigabit: R69 Plus

Best for: Tight budgets that still want a modern network setup

An Allwinner H728 octa-core box on Android 14 with Wi-Fi 6 and Gigabit Ethernet in the specs. The 4GB versions are the sensible choice for a main TV; 2GB + 16GB suits light use.

Buy it if: price matters most but you still want Wi-Fi 6 and a Gigabit port.

5. Budget Amlogic box: Tanix TX5

Best for: Simple streaming on an older TV, local playback via AV/SPDIF

Amlogic S905Y5 on Android 14 with 4K decoding (AV1/VP9/AVS2 up to 4K@60fps listed), dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Ethernet, AV and SPDIF coaxial outputs. Configurations up to 4GB + 64GB.

Video output (as listed): HDMI, 4K decode (AV1/VP9/AVS2 up to 4K@60fps)

Buy it if: you want a low-cost, well-understood Amlogic box with legacy audio/video outputs.

6. Budget stick: HS89 T15

Best for: Hotels, travel, or a TV with no shelf space

An HDMI stick with a Rockchip RK3539 on Android 14 and Wi-Fi 6, offered in 2GB + 16GB and 4GB + 32GB. There is no Ethernet port, so place your router within good Wi-Fi range.

Buy it if: you want something that hides behind the TV and plugs straight into HDMI.

What to avoid in 2026

  • “8K” boxes with very little RAM. The output resolution does not matter if the home screen stutters.
  • Old Android versions with no updates. Apps drop support for old Android releases over time.
  • Listings that sell “free channels” or content access. Buy hardware from sellers who list real specs and a clear warranty and returns policy.
  • 100Mbps Ethernet sold as “high-speed”. It is adequate for streaming, but it is not fast for large local files.

FAQ

Do I need an 8K Android TV box in 2026?

For most people, no. Very little 8K content is available, so buy for smooth 4K playback today. Treat 8K output as a bonus, not the deciding spec.

How much RAM should an Android TV box have?

For a main living-room TV with several apps installed, choose 4GB where the model offers it. 2GB configurations are fine for lighter, single-app use such as a bedroom or travel TV.

Does Gigabit Ethernet matter?

For online streaming a stable 100Mbps port is usually enough. Gigabit helps when you play large local files from a NAS or home server. Check the Ethernet line on each product page.

Will streaming apps play in 4K on these boxes?

Maximum streaming resolution is decided by each app and by the device’s DRM certification, not only by the box hardware. We do not promise a specific resolution for any third-party app.

Do these boxes include channels or subscriptions?

No. CRTLU Digital sells hardware only. You install official apps and sign in with accounts you own. We do not sell content or channel services.
